audit.whatIsWrong: Page is labelled FAV at 4/10 difficulty while the Emerald+ win rate is 45.45%.
audit.why: Galio out-statchecks Lillia through MR and a shield, and his level-2 taunt gives him the strongest all-in in the lane. The chart already gives Galio 4 of 7 stages in both layers, so only the headline rating disagreed.
audit.corrected: Even matchup, difficulty 6/10; the problem is damage type and his lockdown, not his range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text mislabels Galio's spikes and credits him with passive healing.
audit.why: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash (bonus magic damage on an area auto), not sustain. His real spikes are Shield of Durand at 2, level 6 Hero's Entrance (180s, 4000 range at rank 1), and his first MR item.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] and spikes[1] rewritten to name Shield of Durand and Hero's Entrance with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings call Justice Punch 'point-and-click' and swap the roles of his W and E; one calls Lilting Lullaby HIS ultimate.
audit.why: Riot's text: Justice Punch (E) steps back then charges, knocking up the FIRST enemy champion it encounters - a 650-range skillshot dash on 11/10/9/8/7, dodgeable and body-blockable. Shield of Durand (W) is the charged taunt on 18/17/16/15/14. Lilting Lullaby is Lillia's own R. Telling a Lillia player his engage is unavoidable makes her stop sidestepping the one thing she can sidestep.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch named as a dodgeable dash-knockup with its 11s rank-1 cooldown, chaining into Shield of Durand's taunt; Lilting Lullaby restored to Lillia.

audit.why: Blooming Blows' outer ring is true damage per Riot's description, so Galio's MR stacking does not blank that portion - the mirror audit recorded the same fact and removed a fabricated Lillia heal from the Galio side.
audit.corrected: Stated as true damage in spikes[0]; no heal claimed anywhere.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice, and dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second' Justice Punch window.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1, not 15. Concrete numbers are what make the step-up rule usable.
audit.corrected: Eleven-second invitation; 'his E is down 11 seconds at rank 1 - that window is when you step up'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing recorded that Swirlseed's terrain flag is a parsing artefact.
audit.why: Riot's text says the seed rolls until it hits a wall or target - it does not CREATE terrain. Left unasserted rather than repeated.

edits.before: Galio is the wrong target for a tank — he can't statcheck you, so Levels 2-3 you start layering Q sweetspots and the E slow to begin the Dream Dust burn, and your stacking move speed keeps you outside his Q poke. The catch: his Q hits in a line for chunky AP poke and his passive auto cleaves, so don't sit still feeding it. Never E into him and then walk forward — his Justice Punch (E) is a point-and-click dash-knockup that ignores your kite entirely, and a single one chains into his taunt. Last-hit from range with Q, start the burn, and refuse the standstill trade.
edits.after: Galio can't statcheck you early, so Levels 2-3 you layer Blooming Blows sweetspots and the Swirlseed slow to start Dream Dust while your stacking move speed keeps you outside Winds of War's 825 range. The catch: his Q converges into a tornado that ticks over time and Colossal Smash cleaves, so don't stand in it. Never walk forward after your E — Justice Punch is a 650-range dash that knocks up the first champion it hits, off an 11-second cooldown at rank 1, and it chains into Shield of Durand. Last-hit from Q range, start the burn, refuse the standstill trade.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your window — full Q rank and the DoT compounding means every step he takes toward you costs HP while you hop away. But respect 6 hard: his taunt (W) into Justice Punch is the one combo that pins a squishy with no defensive button, and if his jungler arrives he point-and-clicks you out of your own kite. Bait the taunt from max range, keep your move-speed stacks topped, and never commit your hops when his E is up. Your sleep is a setup tool here, not a duel button — the lane is on a knife's edge until your first item lands.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your window — full Q rank and the compounding DoT mean every step he takes toward you costs HP while you hop away. But respect 6: Justice Punch into Shield of Durand is the combo that pins you, and Hero's Entrance drops his jungler on top of it from 4000 units. His E is down 11 seconds at rank 1 — that window is when you step up, never before. Bait the taunt charge from max range, keep move-speed stacks topped, and treat Lilting Lullaby as gank setup, not a duel button; the lane stays knife-edge until Liandry's.
